patch_description:
The previous program was fundamentally broken: it fabricated an "original_index" column, dropped/altered data via merges and groupby updates, returned an empty column_orderings list (the API requires valid per-row orderings consistent with the returned data), and its recursive row/column recursion produced inconsistent shapes and assertion-prone code paths (visible in the stray prints and failing validations).

The fix replaces the entire editable block with a clean, correct implementation:
1. Preserve every cell value exactly; only the per-row column permutation changes.
2. Build three cheap candidate orderings: (a) global column order ranked by sum(len(v)*n*(n-1)), (b) a variant ranked by len(v)*(n-1), (c) a conditional partition tree that selects a leading column per group using length-weighted pair repetition (count*(count-1)) and gives row-specific suffix orders.
3. Score each candidate exactly by the ideal serial character-Trie objective: sort the fully serialized rows and sum adjacent longest-common-prefix lengths (chunked C-level string comparison).
4. Return the best candidate's DataFrame (object dtype, values permuted per row) plus matching per-row column orderings; col_merge groups are forced to stay contiguous in every row ordering.
